profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Its two relevant lines of business are a decades-old, much larger physical and digital records-management segment operating out of a large number of facilities nationally (Wikipedia describes more than 1,500 such facilities), and a newer data center REIT segment built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers.

This address, 4330 South Grove Road in Spokane, Washington, is tagged in source mapping data as an Iron Mountain data center, but Iron Mountain's own data center site does not list any Washington state or Spokane location among its roughly 30 marketed global facilities; its North American list names Boston, Chicago (Des Plaines, IL), Denver, Kansas City, Miami, New Jersey, Ohio, Western Pennsylvania, Phoenix, Richmond, Scottsdale, and Northern Virginia, and no Pacific Northwest site. Nor was Spokane part of the 2018 IO Data Centers acquisition, which added only New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona facilities per Wikipedia's account of that deal.

This registry records that gap honestly rather than asserting data-center specifications that have not been found: no IT capacity, square footage, year opened, or tier certification for this Spokane address was located in operator or public sourcing this session. Given Iron Mountain's much larger records-management business operates a large national facility footprint that is not individually listed on the company's public website, this address is plausibly (though unconfirmed) a records-management or shredding facility rather than a colocation data center, or could reflect an outdated or mistaken mapping-data tag. Confirming this facility's actual status and function would require direct verification with Iron Mountain or a Spokane County Assessor property lookup, neither of which this registry has completed.

This facility is listed as Iron Mountain's sole location in Spokane County on the operator's official site locator, but the research notes indicate it appears to be a records storage facility rather than a computing data center. No IT load, power capacity, or cooling specifications are published for this address. The distinction matters because Iron Mountain operates both legacy records management buildings and newer hyperscale data center campuses under one corporate name, and this row was matched to a records storage location finder rather than a data center inventory.

Washington state has 46 mapped facilities across the AI infrastructure landscape, but only two publish power figures totaling 60 MW. This campus ranks third by published capacity in the state, which means no power specification has been published for it. Without a megawatt figure, the computing potential cannot be calculated in terms of racks or accelerators.

If this is a records storage facility as the research suggests, it does not contribute to AI-capable compute infrastructure.
